did: The server's PR gate used to hold a runner for up to an hour while it polled every other check. Now short jobs decide it: one when the pull request changes, and one each time another check finishes, so no runner waits and a re-run of a failed check updates the gate by itself. It was proven red then green on its own pull request and on RR22's #770, where a failure turned green twenty seconds after a re-run with nobody touching the gate. Review found and I fixed five real bugs along the way, the last one live: when CodeQL finished last, the gate stayed pending, so a second pull request fixed that and added a sweep you can run by hand. The fifteen-minute schedule meant as a backstop has never fired, and that is filed for you as #772.

calls.title: Keep the sixty-minute limit, per run, though #762 said it goes away
options: Keep it per run, so nothing passes that used to fail
calls.why: The run's rule was that no pull request may go green that would have been red before, and dropping the limit would let a sixty-one-minute run pass.
calls.undo: Remove the over-an-hour check in judge() in scripts/pr_gate.py and its self-tests.

calls.title: Fall back to waiting in the job when main's listener can't hear every workflow
options: No fallback, leaving the gate pending on such pull requests
Fall back to waiting in the job, as before
calls.why: GitHub runs main's copy of the verdict workflow, so the pull request that adds it, or adds a new workflow, would otherwise never be decided.
calls.undo: Drop the base_listens branch and wait() from open_gate() in scripts/pr_gate.py.

calls.title: A check_run trigger for other apps' checks, later found dead
options: Also trigger on check_run from other apps
calls.why: It was meant to hear code scanning's CodeQL check; review then showed GitHub never fires it for commits GitHub Actions runs on, so it was removed and replaced by the sweep.
calls.undo: Already removed in #767; nothing to undo.

calls.title: A fifteen-minute sweep that re-judges unfinished gates
options: Document that a gate can stay pending and file a follow-up
Add a scheduled sweep that dispatches re-judging
Keep polling in a job while other apps' checks run
calls.why: The point of the change is that nobody babysits the gate; the coordinator chose it, at 96 short runs a day.
calls.undo: Remove the schedule and the sweep job from gate-verdict.yml and sweep() from scripts/pr_gate.py.

calls.title: Let the sweep be run by hand from an empty dispatch
options: Prove the sweep only on its schedule
A separate workflow for a manual sweep
An empty dispatch of the verdict workflow runs the sweep
calls.why: The schedule never fired, so this was the only way to prove the sweep works, and it gives a sweep-now button.
calls.undo: Make the dispatch inputs required again and restore the jobs' if: lines in gate-verdict.yml.

left: The fifteen-minute schedule has never fired, even after the workflow was re-pushed; it waits on you to check the repository's Actions settings, issue #772.
A pull request whose last check is CodeQL hasn't yet been seen deciding its own gate on the fixed path; the next one to finish that way shows it.
The branch claude/pr-gate-event-driven-762-pending needs deleting; this session's proxy refuses branch deletes.
Old pull requests #301, #340, #392 and #769 now carry a PR gate check from the first sweep; it is accurate, but you'll see it there.
